samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the finite precision of floating-point representations can introduce rounding errors during intermediate calculations. When adding three numbers, the order in which operations are performed can affect which intermediate results are rounded, leading to different final outcomes. For example, (a + b) + c may yield a different result than a + (b + c) due to differing rounding at each step.

Floating-point addition is not associative because rounding errors introduced during each operation can accumulate differently depending on the order of computation. For example, adding a very small number to a large number may result in no change due to limited precision, but the outcome can vary if the order of operations is altered. This means that (a + b) + c may not equal a + (b + c) when using finite-precision floating-point arithmetic.
